To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
apamin-sensitive Ca2+-activated K+ channels are located on bovine chromaffins cells and that they regulate the release of catecolamines evoked by a variety of physiological agonists.

apamin-sensitive small-conductance calcium-dependent potassium channels are present in chromaffin cells at a density of approximately 900 channels/cell and that these channels are involved in regulating secretion.

apamin-sensitive Ca2+ activated K+ (SK) channels, with a density of about 900 per single bovine adrenal medullary chromaffin cell (0.72 channels per micron 2), regulate some of the electrical events in chromaffin cells, and thus indirectly, the opening and closing of voltage-dependent Ca(2+) channels, the entry of Ca2+ into the cells and the rate of exocytosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of SK channels in the control of Ca2+ homeostasis, secretion and electrical properties of chromaffin and other neuroendocrine cells.
the role of the small conductance Ca2+-activated K+ (SK) channels in the regulation of catechol amine release from chromaffin cells.
the study of the molecular mechanisms of the regulation of the release of catecolamines from the adrenal medulla.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the SK channels of chromaffin cell membranes have a major impact on the secretory process, and that the density of these channels (900 per cell) is high enough to exert a powerful effect on the secretory machinery of chromaffin granules.

apamin-sensitive SK channels are present in chromaffin cells at a density of approx. 900 channels per cell, and that these channels control a significant portion of the electrical activity and the rate of secretion of catecholines.

apamin-sensitive SK channels in the adrenal medulla chromatin cells play an essential role in controlling the electrical properties of the cells, the release of cate-cholamines and the [Ca2+] in the cytosol.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SK channels are a key component in the regulation of the secretory activity of chromaffins cells.
the SK channels play an important role in the regulation of catecholaminergic secretion.
the density of SK channels in chromaffin cells is very high, that they are involved in the regulation of catecholaminergic secretion and that they are the main target of the toxin apamin.
The main takeaway from our work is that

apamin-sensitive SK channels are present in high densities in chromaffin cells, that they are functionally coupled to the release machinery and that they can be modulated by the physiological agonists of chromaffin cell secretion.
apamin-sensitive SK channels are present in chromaffin cells at a very high density (approx. 900 channels per cell) and that they play a role in the control of catecholaminergic secretion.
the SK channel blocker apamin is an effective secretagogue for adrenal medullary chromaffin cells.
